speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
text: asked the Minister for Health in light of the Government's intention to include mental health under the Healthier SG initiative, whether the Ministry will consider providing subventions for citizens in need of community counselling, particularly in addressing issues, such as caregiver stress.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: My response will also cover the matters raised in the question by Dr Lim Wee Kiak1 which are scheduled for a subsequent Sitting.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Dr Lim Wee Kiak is not here but I hope he gets to read my answer and if it answers his question, he may want to withdraw his question for a future Sitting.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We are commencing national Healthier SG enrolment from 5 July this year.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: In providing care to residents with chronic conditions under Healthier SG, family doctors will be guided by care protocols.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We have, so far, developed 12 such protocols.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Every one of them requires significant consultation, coordination, preparation as well as training.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We will expand the coverage and intend to cover mental health in due course.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: In any case, Healthier SG is not the only avenue to care for residents experiencing mental health issues.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Under the Community Mental Health Masterplan, we work with social service agencies to set up community outreach and intervention teams to support persons with mental health needs as well as their caregivers.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: This includes educating caregivers on stress management and self-care, linking them with counselling services and support groups when needed.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: And the Ministry of Health (MOH) provides full funding to these teams, and residents that can access their services and support at no cost.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: As Healthier SG is progressively rolled out and stabilised, it is possible for residents to receive annual health reports, as suggested by Dr Lim Wee Kiak.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: With Healthier SG, enrolled residents will have access to a personalised Health Plan via their HealthHub mobile application or the web portal.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: If the resident is diligent with his health screening, he will also have access via HealthHub to his latest health screening results.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We will monitor the usage of such information on HealthHub and explore how we can further enhance it to support residents' health journeys.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Deputy Speaker, I thank the Minister for the very positive updates on the number that had already been pre-enrolled.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Some of my Jalan Kayu residents, having heard about Healthier SG, especially the younger ones, who know that chronic disease risk can start from 40 years old and seeing that those with chronic disease can be pre-enrolled, asked if in the course of the year – they understand the phases and the need to prioritise our seniors – should they happen to be in a GP clinic and the GP clinic has the capacity to enrol them, can they be more proactive and be allowed to enrol?

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: So, the question is: if they happen to be in a GP clinic for the next one year before their phase comes, and the GP clinic has the capacity to enrol them, can they be considered?

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The second supplementary question is that some of my more senior residents who have been seeing polyclinic doctors for their chronic disease management are quite convinced that GP clinics may be closer to their home and, as they age, mobility issues come in, and being enrolled will be good.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: So, they are asking whether their out-of-pocket expenditure, when they go to the GP clinic for their regular follow-up visits, will the consultation fee and medication fee be also managed and be close to what they are paying for at the polyclinics?

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: In any case, Healthier SG is about MOH as well as the health ecosystem doing more to help people to take care of their own health.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, for young residents, I will encourage them, with or without the Government's explicit support, they can always do more to lead a healthier lifestyle.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: And I think the young are increasingly mindful of that.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: There is a lot they can do here – eat less sugar, eat less salt and have less device time – to start with.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I do know that because of rising healthcare needs plus Healthier SG, costs can increase.
